pr_body:
Implements a chunk of apple native-api based globalization. 

**Old, icu-based private API:** 

- GlobalizationNative_StartsWith
- GlobalizationNative_EndsWith
- GlobalizationNative_IndexOf
- GlobalizationNative_LastIndexOf

**New, non-icu private API:** 

- GlobalizationNative_StartsWithNative
- GlobalizationNative_EndsWithNative
- GlobalizationNative_IndexOfNative _// will be called also for LastIndexOf_


**Affected public API :**

- CompareInfo.IsPrefix
- CompareInfo.IsSuffix
- String.StartsWith
- String.EndsWith
- CompareInfo.IndexOf
- CompareInfo.LastIndexOf
- String.IndexOf
- String.LastIndexOf

**APIs that will not be supported**

- CompareInfo.GetSortKey
- CompareInfo.GetSortKeyLength
- CompareInfo.GetHashCode

Fixes [#86699](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/86699)
Contributes to https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/80689
cc @SamMonoRT

issue_context.title: [OSX] HybridGlobalization implement collation native functions
issue_context.body:
Implement collation functions for OSX platforms.

        

- [ ] GlobalizationNative_GetSortHandle

        
        - return reference to NSLocale
        
     

- [ ]    GlobalizationNative_CloseSortHandle

        
        - release reference to NSLocale
        
      

- [x]   GlobalizationNative_CompareString

        
        - [NSString compare:options:range:locale:](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsstring/1414561-compare?language=objc)
   
      

- [ ]   GlobalizationNative_IndexOf

        
        - [NSString rangeOfString:options:range:locale:](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/foundation/nsstring/1417348-rangeofstring?language=objc)
        
    

- [ ]     GlobalizationNative_LastIndexOf

        
        - same as GlobalizationNative_IndexOf w/ NSBackwardsSearch
        
    

- [ ]     GlobalizationNative_StartsWith

        
        - can be implemented trough GlobalizationNative_CompareString?
        

- [ ]      GlobalizationNative_EndsWith

        
        - can be implemented trough GlobalizationNative_CompareString?
        
    

- [ ]     GlobalizationNative_GetSortKey

        
        - wcsxfrm_l?
        
  

- [ ]       GlobalizationNative_GetSortVersion

        
        - ??

Contributes to #80689

review_comments: Why these cases are excluded, what is the output here? Is it -1 like with `CompareOptions.None` when using ICU? Should we add these cases to the documentation?
Yes, I will add them in the documentation. Output is -1 here.
Documentation needs a mention of this, might be even "behaves as described for WASM".
Out of curiosity, why are we adding `NoInlining` here and on `StartsWithNative` but not on the other ones?

I did like is done for `ICU` https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/main/src/libraries/Common/src/Interop/Interop.Collation.cs#L34

But not sure why only these 2 functions have `MethodImplOptions.NoInlining`
My guess is that it is to avoid regressing the hot path of the method by inlining the PInvoke.
The code to set `matchLengthPtr` in `CompareInfo.ICU.cs` and `CompareInfo.OSX.cs` suggests that OSX does support match length.
`matchLengthPtr` is sen on `OSX` only for `IndexOf`, `LasIndexOf` functions. For `IsPrefix` and `IsSuffix` functions for now it will not be supported on `OSX`.

Are they not implementable or will they be added in a follow up PR?

If the former, why is that? It wouldn't be for the same reason as wasm, would it? If its for a different reason, I think we should use a different PNSE string.

If the latter, the logic afterwards from `StartsWithCore` flow through `IcuStartsWith` in which we already have logic for apple right?
```
#if TARGET_OSX || TARGET_MACCATALYST || TARGET_IOS || TARGET_TVOS
                if (GlobalizationMode.Hybrid)
                    return NativeStartsWith(pPrefix, prefix.Length, pSource, source.Length, options);
#endif
```
If done in a later PR, can we still use a different block and not throw the `SR.PlatformNotSupported_HybridGlobalizationWithMatchLength` and maybe put a tracking link so we don't forget this PNSE addition?

To get the correct `matchLengthPtr` locale-aware search is needed which is not supported for all cases on `OSX`.
Users will be interested in this  `matchLengthPtr` mostly when in the source string and target string letters have different representations, which is not implementable on `OSX` (this cases are also in IndexOf function). 
So with my current research I would say it is not implementable and reason is same as on WASM Linguistic comparison is not supported.

As @ilonatommy mentioned in below conversation
When disabling `matchLengthPtr` for WASM they did a research on frequency of usage of this parameter on GitHub out of our runtime libs and `matchLengthPtr` is used very rarely.

Yes it is not supported because we normalize the strings before checking `IsPrefix` or `IsSuffix`.

Implementing through iteration will create same issues (not covered cases) that we have in `IndexOf` function and will be way more slower.
One more solution will be to call `IndexOf` function inside `IsPrefix` for example. 
But note that doing this we will loose full coverage of cases for `IsPrefix` and `IsSuffix` functions and have more complex implementation. For further investigation I have created ticket already https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/87767
I prefer to keep current implementation and not support `matchLengthPtr` for now as it is not so used parameter.
The code to set `matchLengthPtr` in `CompareInfo.ICU.cs` and `CompareInfo.OSX.cs` suggests that OSX does support match length.
`matchLengthPtr` is set on `OSX` only for `IndexOf`, `LasIndexOf` functions. For `IsPrefix` and `IsSuffix` functions for now it will not be supported on `OSX`.

If it's supported for `IndexOf` and `LastIndexOf` then why not to use e.g. `IndexOf` inside the `IsPrefix` impelementation and if the result == 0 then return true for being the prefix + use the `matchLengthPtr` value, otherwise: false.
OSX's implementation of `IndexOf` will surely take more computing than `IsPrefix` so we could do it only when the user actually passed a non-null pointer to `matchLengthPtr`.

On `OSX` `IndexOf` and `LastIndexOf` linguistic comparison is not fully covered. I tried to cover all possible cases. But in cases when `source` and `prefix` will contain letters with different char lengths they will not work correctly (more about covered / not covered cases is written in doc) 
I prefer to go with current implementation and not support  `matchLengthPtr` for `IsPrefix` and `IsSuffix` as using `IndexOf` will not give correct `matchLengthPtr` for all cases and can even return`false` for some cases when it should be `true`.

In the future when all these missing cases will be covered that is a good idea to call `IndexOf` inside `IsPrefix`.

I missed the fact that `IsPrefix` has wider linguistic support than `IndexOf`. If it's like that, then I would vote for unifying both to `IsPrefix` and removing the support for `matchLengthPtr` for IOS. When disabling `matchLengthPtr` for WASM we did a research on frequency of usage of this parameter on GitHub out of our runtime libs and it is used very rarely.

I believe that from this reason, it is more important to support linguistic comparison on the highest level we can, even at the cost of blocking this API for IOS's Hybrid. We can do it in the next PR where we will measure also which approach is less computing-costly.
I have opened https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/87767 for future investigation.
